# DesignSystem architecture

**Date:** 2026-06-14
**Status:** design — approved spine, awaiting review before CUE authoring
**Scope:** architecture only. No primitives are specified or generated by this
document. It defines *how* crest-synth's reusable UI components are structured
so that, when a view needs a component, we author it consistently.

## Problem

crest-synth will grow many views (the mixer is the first; editors, browsers,
parameter panels follow). Each view needs common building blocks — value
displays, lists, grids, panels, menus, popovers. We do not want to reinvent
these per view, and we do not want them to drift apart as the app grows. We
want a small, consistent base that composes into views.

## Non-goals / explicit constraints

- **We build only what a view actually needs, when it needs it.** There is no
  target catalog of N components. The vocabulary below is for naming
  consistency, not a build list.
- **We vendor nothing and depend on no external UI crate.** Everything is
  authored as CUE and generated by the crest-spec loop, like the rest of the
  crate. The prior art cited below is *inspiration only* — patterns we apply to
  our own generated components. No external code enters the tree.
- This is a `crest-spec` project: we author the spec, never hand-write the
  `.rs`. This doc is the prose rationale; the machine spec is a `DesignSystem`
  CUE context authored afterward.

## Prior art (inspiration, not dependencies)

- **JUCE `Component` + `LookAndFeel`** — a control owns only behavior; a
  separate, swappable object owns *all* drawing and cascades to children.
  Re-skin the whole app by swapping one object, with zero behavior change. This
  is the canonical pattern for dense *audio* tools and the highest-leverage idea
  here. (Same split recurs in Radix headless-vs-styling, Unity UXML/USS/C#,
  Godot `Control` + `Theme`.)
- **Ark UI / Zag.js** — component behavior modeled as a pure state machine,
  projected into a host-neutral view-model via `connect()`, with the renderer as
  a swappable adapter. This is the one idea in the web lineage that survives
  leaving the browser — and it is essentially what `MixerView` already is.
- **Blender** — stays consistent by keeping a *tiny* shared primitive set (a
  slider is a styled number field, not a separate widget) and one global theme.
  Lesson: collapse near-duplicate controls into one primitive with variants.
- **Enterprise systems (Spectrum, Polaris, Carbon, Atlassian, Material)** all
  converge on `Tokens → Foundations → Primitives → Components → Patterns/Views`,
  with one load-bearing rule: components reference only *semantic* tokens, never
  raw values. That is what makes restyling/theming free later.

## Architecture

### Layer model (mapped onto crest-synth's CUE/DDD constructs)

| DS layer | What it is | crest-synth construct |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Tokens** | semantic design decisions (color, spacing, focus, type) | value objects in a new `DesignSystem` context |
| **Behavior primitives** | one pure reducer per control (`State` + `Event` + `apply`) | aggregate / value-object — the `MixerView` shape |
| **Skin** | egui drawing, parameterized by a `Theme`, reading only tokens | a `Theme` port + egui adapter assets |
| **Components** | composed primitives (channel strip, transport) | aggregates composing primitives |
| **Views** | full screens | top-level assets (`MixerView` is the first) |

Dependencies point downward only — which is the project's DIP rule, for free.

### The load-bearing decision: behavior ÷ skin ÷ token

Every primitive is three parts, and the split is the whole game:

1. **Behavior** — a pure reducer: `State` + an `Event` enum + `apply(&mut self,
   Event)`. No egui, no I/O. Unit-tested headlessly by feeding events and
   asserting state — identical to how `mixer.cue` already proves `MixerView`.
   This is simultaneously the Ark/Zag "state machine" and what we already build.
2. **View-model projection** — `fn view_model(&State) -> Vm` producing
   host-neutral parts (role, value, focus/disabled flags, label). This is Zag's
   `connect()`: it decouples behavior from egui, so the same primitive could
   later render in a TUI or a test harness.
3. **Skin** — `fn draw(ui, vm, theme: &Theme)`: the *only* part that touches
   egui, parameterized by a `Theme` that exposes only semantic tokens. Swap the
   `Theme` → restyle the whole app, zero behavior change. This is JUCE's
   `LookAndFeel`, in egui.

So a `ValueControl`'s behavior knows nothing about pixels; its skin knows
nothing about mute-vs-volume; the `Theme` is the only place a literal color
lives.

### Consistency invariants (what keeps the generate-loop from drifting)

Authored as `DesignSystem` invariants, mirroring the style already in
`mixer.cue`:

- Every interactive primitive is a pure reducer (`State` + `Event` + `apply`);
  its behavior layer never touches egui.
- Every skin reads only semantic tokens — no literal colors or sizes in draw
  code.
- Every primitive is proven headlessly (events in, state asserted) with no
  window — the existing mixer-demo pattern.
- Navigation is semantic events shared by keyboard and gamepad (the existing
  `MixerViewEvent` precedent).

## Tokens (scoped to what the mixer renders today)

Two tiers. Skins read **only** the semantic tier; the `Theme` binds semantic →
raw.

- **Raw tier** — literal values (a small palette of colors, a few spacing/size
  units). No component names these.
- **Semantic tier** — only the intents the mixer needs now:
  - `focus_ring` — the focused cell
  - `edit_active` — focused **and** in edit mode (the `> … <` state)
  - `value_fill` — the value-bar / readout fill
  - `meter_peak` — the live peak overlay on the Volume row
  - `toggle_on` / `toggle_off` — mute/solo states
  - `text_default` / `text_muted`
  - `panel_bg` / `separator`

The set grows one entry at a time when a new view needs one — never
preemptively.

## Keyboard/controller focus model

The web design systems have nothing for this; we design it ourselves, and
deliberately avoid building a general "focus engine":

- **Traversal + mode stay in the view reducer.** `MixerView` already owns the
  cursor `(channel, param)`, edit-mode, and edge-scrolling, because traversal
  rules are layout-specific (a 2D channel×param grid scrolls differently than a
  future 1D list). Each view owns its own traversal, as `MixerView` does now. We
  do not build a shared traversal engine.
- **Primitives are mode-agnostic and only *report* focus.** A primitive's
  view-model carries `focused: bool` and `editing: bool`. It does not know how it
  got focused. The skin renders those two flags via `focus_ring` / `edit_active`.
  That is the only thing that must be consistent across every primitive — and it
  is, because it is one skin rule, not N implementations.

This is exactly what the draw code does today (`is_focused_cell`, `edit_mode`
passed into `draw_param_row`); we are naming it as a contract instead of an
ad-hoc argument list.

## Worked example: the mixer, decomposed

The existing mixer view, read through this architecture, already implies:

- a **ValueControl** primitive (the Vol/Rvb/Ech/Pan rows): normalized value,
  `focused`/`editing` flags, optional `meter_peak` overlay (Volume row);
- a **Toggle** primitive (Mute/Solo rows): bool, `focused` flag;
- a **Strip/Panel** container (the vertical channel column);
- focus/cursor traversal owned by `MixerView` (already implemented).

Nothing else is needed for the mixer. When we author the `DesignSystem` context,
`ValueControl` + `Toggle` + the focus contract are the natural first primitives,
and refactoring the mixer to consume them is the proof the stack works.

## Next step

After review, author the `DesignSystem` CUE context (tokens as value objects,
the `Theme` port, the behavior÷skin÷token contracts and invariants), then spec
the first primitives only as the mixer requires them. No primitive is generated
ahead of a view that needs it.
